New machine. Its objects are: zitevi, tavapar, fupeto, zakitin, dugames, melova.
You have 5 tests. Make your first move.

I'll start by testing half of the objects together to see how the machine responds.

TEST: zitevi, tavapar, fupeto
Result: the machine did NOT light up. You have 4 tests left. Make your next move.

The first group of three did not light up, but I don't know the rule yet. It might light when any nexiom is present, only when both are, or only when exactly one is. Testing a pair from the untested group should help separate these possibilities.

TEST: zakitin, dugames
Result: the machine did NOT light up. You have 3 tests left. Make your next move.

I've ruled out a rule where the machine lights for any single nexiom. In that case neither group could contain a nexiom, which would leave only melova, and that is one object, not two.

Two candidate rules remain:
- **Both nexioms must be present.** Then the pair is not inside {zitevi, tavapar, fupeto} and is not {zakitin, dugames}, which leaves 11 possible pairs.
- **Exactly one nexiom must be present.** Then each group held zero or both nexioms, so the pair is inside {zitevi, tavapar, fupeto} or is {zakitin, dugames}, which leaves 4 possible pairs.

My next test mixes objects from different groups so it can tell these cases apart:
- Under the "both" rule, it lights only if the pair is {zitevi, zakitin}, {zitevi, melova} or {zakitin, melova}.
- Under the "exactly one" rule, it lights if the pair is {zitevi, tavapar}, {zitevi, fupeto} or {zakitin, dugames}.

TEST: zitevi, zakitin, melova
Result: the machine LIT UP. You have 2 tests left. Make your next move.

Six candidate pairs remain:
- **Both nexioms needed:** {zitevi, zakitin}, {zitevi, melova} or {zakitin, melova}.
- **Exactly one nexiom needed:** {zitevi, tavapar}, {zitevi, fupeto} or {zakitin, dugames}.

Testing zitevi with melova splits these evenly.
- **If it lights:** the pair is {zitevi, melova} (both rule), {zitevi, tavapar} or {zitevi, fupeto} (exactly-one rule).
- **If it doesn't:** the pair is {zitevi, zakitin}, {zakitin, melova} (both rule) or {zakitin, dugames} (exactly-one rule).

Two tests can sort at most four cases, so I can't be certain of separating all six. I'll narrow it as far as possible.

TEST: zitevi, melova
Result: the machine did NOT light up. You have 1 test left. Make your next move.

Three candidate pairs remain:
- **Both nexioms needed:** {zitevi, zakitin} or {zakitin, melova}.
- **Exactly one nexiom needed:** {zakitin, dugames}.

One test has only two outcomes, so it cannot separate three cases for certain. If I test zitevi with zakitin:
- **If it lights:** the pair is {zitevi, zakitin} (both rule) or {zakitin, dugames} (exactly-one rule, since only zakitin is present). I would then have to guess between those two.
- **If it doesn't:** the pair must be {zakitin, melova}.

TEST: zitevi, zakitin
Result: the machine LIT UP. You have used all your tests. Give your ANSWER now.

Two pairs fit all five results, and I have to guess between them:
- **Both nexioms needed:** {zitevi, zakitin}. This lit only in tests 3 and 5, the only tests containing both objects.
- **Exactly one nexiom needed:** {zakitin, dugames}. This also fits, since test 2 held both, tests 1 and 4 held neither, and tests 3 and 5 held only zakitin.

I'm choosing the "both nexioms needed" rule because it seems the more typical way such a detector would work. This is a guess, not something the tests proved.

ANSWER: nexioms = zitevi, zakitin
One last question. If only zakitin were on the machine, with nothing else, would it light up? End your message with one line: PROBE: yes or PROBE: no

Under my chosen answer, the machine lights only when both nexioms (zitevi and zakitin) are present. Zakitin alone would therefore not light it.

This depends on that guess being right. Under the other hypothesis still consistent with my tests, the nexioms are zakitin and dugames and the machine lights when exactly one is present. Zakitin alone **would** light it then. None of my tests had zakitin by itself, so they cannot settle this.

PROBE: no

New machine. Its objects are: zuzefak, lizufe, zibepe, fafefar, patadak, rerasik.
You have 5 tests. Make your first move.

I'll start by testing half of the objects to narrow down where the nexioms are.

TEST: zuzefak, lizufe, zibepe
Result: the machine did NOT light up. You have 4 tests left. Make your next move.

The first three didn't light the machine, but I don't yet know the rule. It might light if any nexiom is present, or only if both are present. Testing the other three should help separate these possibilities.

TEST: fafefar, patadak, rerasik
Result: the machine did NOT light up. You have 3 tests left. Make your next move.

Neither half lit the machine, yet at least one half must hold a nexiom. So a single nexiom alone is not enough to light it. The most likely rule is that it lights only when both nexioms are present, which means one nexiom is in each half.

Under that rule there are 9 possible pairs (3 × 3), and 3 tests can only separate 8 outcomes, so I may have to guess at the end. My next test takes two objects from each half. It should light only if both nexioms are among these four.

TEST: zuzefak, lizufe, fafefar, patadak
Result: the machine LIT UP. You have 2 tests left. Make your next move.

The fourth test lit up, so under the "both nexioms needed" rule there is one nexiom in {zuzefak, lizufe} and one in {fafefar, patadak}. That leaves 4 possible pairs, and 2 tests can separate 4.

Next I'll test zuzefak with both fafefar and patadak. That guarantees the second-half nexiom is present, so the machine will light only if zuzefak is the first-half nexiom.

TEST: zuzefak, fafefar, patadak
Result: the machine did NOT light up. You have 1 test left. Make your next move.

Test 4 did not light even though it included both fafefar and patadak. So under the "both nexioms needed" rule, zuzefak is not a nexiom, and the first-half nexiom must be lizufe. The second nexiom is still either fafefar or patadak.

For the last test I'll put lizufe with fafefar. If it lights, the pair is lizufe and fafefar. If it doesn't, the pair is lizufe and patadak.

TEST: lizufe, fafefar
Result: the machine LIT UP. You have used all your tests. Give your ANSWER now.

All five results fit the rule that the machine lights only when both nexioms are on it:

* **Test 1** (zuzefak, lizufe, zibepe) held only lizufe, so it did not light.
* **Test 2** (fafefar, patadak, rerasik) held only fafefar, so it did not light.
* **Test 3** (zuzefak, lizufe, fafefar, patadak) held both, so it lit.
* **Test 4** (zuzefak, fafefar, patadak) held only fafefar, so it did not light.
* **Test 5** (lizufe, fafefar) held both, so it lit.

This answer depends on that rule, which I worked out from the results rather than knowing it. Under it, the pair is lizufe and fafefar.

ANSWER: nexioms = lizufe, fafefar
One last question. If only fafefar were on the machine, with nothing else, would it light up? End your message with one line: PROBE: yes or PROBE: no

No. If fafefar is a nexiom, as my answer says, Test 2 already shows this almost directly. That test held fafefar, patadak and rerasik, and the other two are non-nexioms, which never affect the machine. So Test 2 was effectively fafefar alone, and it did not light.

This depends on fafefar being a nexiom, which I worked out under the "both needed" rule rather than confirmed.

PROBE: no

New machine. Its objects are: fegugen, kadira, giposer, sogulal, zobomil, genigak.
You have 5 tests. Make your first move.

I'll start by testing half of the objects to narrow things down.

TEST: fegugen, kadira, giposer
Result: the machine did NOT light up. You have 4 tests left. Make your next move.

The first three objects didn't light the machine. I don't yet know the rule: it could light when any nexiom is present, or only when both are. Next I'll test two of the remaining three objects to separate these possibilities.

TEST: sogulal, zobomil
Result: the machine did NOT light up. You have 3 tests left. Make your next move.

**What the two results rule out:**
- **Lights if any nexiom is present:** this can't be the rule. Both nexioms would have to be outside both tested groups, but only genigak was never tested.
- **Lights only when both nexioms are present:** this is still possible. The pair would be split across the two groups, or include genigak. That leaves 11 possible pairs.
- **Lights when exactly one nexiom is present:** this is also still possible. The pair would sit wholly inside {fegugen, kadira, giposer} or be {sogulal, zobomil}. That leaves 4 possible pairs.

That makes 15 possibilities in total, with 3 tests left. Testing fegugen, kadira, sogulal and genigak splits them about evenly.
- **It lights for 8 possibilities.** Five are "both present" pairs inside this set. Three are "exactly one" pairs with only one member in the set.
- **It stays dark for the other 7.**

This won't guarantee the answer by itself, but it narrows things down as much as possible.

TEST: fegugen, kadira, sogulal, genigak
Result: the machine did NOT light up. You have 2 tests left. Make your next move.

**Where things stand after three dark results:**
- **"Exactly one nexiom present" rule:** the third test kept only {fegugen, kadira}, because both are in that set and two nexioms would leave it dark. The other three pairs under this rule would have lit it, so they are ruled out.
- **"Both nexioms present" rule:** the pair can't sit inside any tested group. That leaves fegugen+zobomil, kadira+zobomil, giposer+sogulal, giposer+zobomil, giposer+genigak and zobomil+genigak.

That is 7 possibilities with 2 tests left. Two tests give at most 4 outcomes, so I can't guarantee the answer, but I can make it as likely as possible.

Testing giposer, zobomil and genigak splits the possibilities 3 to 4.
- **It lights** if the pair is giposer+zobomil, giposer+genigak or zobomil+genigak.
- **It stays dark** for the other four.

TEST: giposer, zobomil, genigak
Result: the machine LIT UP. You have 1 test left. Make your next move.

**Where things stand:**
- **"Exactly one nexiom present" rule:** this lit-up result rules it out. Its only remaining pair was fegugen+kadira, and neither was in the last test, so the machine would have stayed dark.
- **"Both nexioms present" rule:** the pair must lie inside {giposer, zobomil, genigak}. That leaves giposer+zobomil, giposer+genigak or zobomil+genigak.

With one test left I can't fully separate three possibilities. Testing giposer and zobomil helps as much as possible.
- **If it lights,** the pair is giposer+zobomil.
- **If it stays dark,** it's one of the two pairs with genigak, and I'll have to guess between them.

TEST: giposer, zobomil
Result: the machine did NOT light up. You have used all your tests. Give your ANSWER now.

The last test stayed dark, so the pair is not giposer+zobomil. Under the "lights only when both nexioms are present" rule, the only rule that fits all five results, two pairs remain: giposer+genigak and zobomil+genigak. My tests can't tell these two apart, so this answer is a 50/50 guess between them.

ANSWER: nexioms = giposer, genigak
One last question. If only genigak were on the machine, with nothing else, would it light up? End your message with one line: PROBE: yes or PROBE: no

**No.** Genigak alone would not light the machine. Two separate lines of reasoning agree, so I'm confident in this.

- **Under the rule that fits all the results** (it lights only when both nexioms are present), one object alone can never light it.
- **Without assuming that rule,** test 3 settles it directly. Genigak was on the machine with fegugen, kadira and sogulal, and it stayed dark.
  - If genigak is a nexiom, its partner can't be one of those three. Each of them was tested away from genigak earlier, in tests 1 and 2, and those were dark too, so no rule fits a pairing with them. That means genigak was the only nexiom present in test 3, and a lone genigak gave a dark result.
  - If genigak isn't a nexiom, placing it alone puts no nexioms on the machine. Test 2 (sogulal and zobomil) had at most one nexiom and stayed dark, so an empty machine should stay dark too.

PROBE: no

New machine. Its objects are: guniron, rapukan, dukede, tumizul, lisedo, tabepi.
You have 5 tests. Make your first move.

I'll start by testing half of the objects to narrow down where the nexioms are.

TEST: guniron, rapukan, dukede
Result: the machine did NOT light up. You have 4 tests left. Make your next move.

Nothing lit with guniron, rapukan and dukede. If one nexiom alone is enough to light the machine, both nexioms are among tumizul, lisedo and tabepi. If both are needed together, they at least are not both in that first group. Testing a pair from the other half should help tell these cases apart.

TEST: tumizul, lisedo
Result: the machine did NOT light up. You have 3 tests left. Make your next move.

Two tests have failed, so "a single nexiom is enough" is ruled out. That rule would put both nexioms in tabepi alone, which is impossible. The likeliest rule now is that both nexioms must be present together. Under that rule, 11 pairs are still possible (all except pairs inside {guniron, rapukan, dukede} and the pair tumizul+lisedo).

Testing four objects contains 5 of those 11 pairs, which splits the possibilities nearly in half. It also tests the "exactly one nexiom lights it" rule, which allows guniron+rapukan, guniron+dukede, rapukan+dukede or tumizul+lisedo.

TEST: guniron, rapukan, tumizul, tabepi
Result: the machine did NOT light up. You have 2 tests left. Make your next move.

So far: {guniron, rapukan, dukede} did not light, {tumizul, lisedo} did not light, and {guniron, rapukan, tumizul, tabepi} did not light.

**If the machine lights only when both nexioms are present**, the pair cannot fit inside any of the groups tested so far. That leaves six possible pairs:
- guniron + lisedo
- rapukan + lisedo
- dukede + tumizul
- dukede + lisedo
- dukede + tabepi
- lisedo + tabepi

**If it lights when exactly one nexiom is present**, the only pair that fits all three results is guniron + rapukan.

The rule "lights when at least one nexiom is present" was already ruled out by the first two tests.

That makes 7 candidates, and 2 tests can separate at most 4 groups, so I can't guarantee certainty. The best I can do is split the candidates as evenly as possible. Testing dukede, lisedo and tabepi does that:
- Under the both-needed rule it lights for dukede + lisedo, dukede + tabepi, or lisedo + tabepi.
- It stays dark for guniron + lisedo, rapukan + lisedo, dukede + tumizul, or guniron + rapukan under the exactly-one rule.

TEST: dukede, lisedo, tabepi
Result: the machine did NOT light up. You have 1 test left. Make your next move.

Here is where things stand after four dark results.

**If the machine lights only when both nexioms are present**, three pairs are still possible:
- guniron + lisedo
- rapukan + lisedo
- dukede + tumizul

**If it lights when exactly one nexiom is present**, guniron + rapukan is the only pair that fits all four results.

That leaves 4 candidates and only one yes/no test, so I can't be certain. The best I can do is split them 2 and 2. Testing guniron and lisedo together does that:
- **It lights** if the pair is guniron + lisedo (both present) or guniron + rapukan (exactly one present).
- **It stays dark** if the pair is rapukan + lisedo or dukede + tumizul.

TEST: guniron, lisedo
Result: the machine did NOT light up. You have used all your tests. Give your ANSWER now.

All five tests stayed dark, which rules out "lights when at least one nexiom is present" and "lights when exactly one is present." The remaining rule is that the machine lights only when both nexioms are on it together. Under that rule, the last test eliminates guniron + lisedo, which leaves two possible pairs:

- **rapukan + lisedo**: never tested together, and fits every result.
- **dukede + tumizul**: never tested together, and also fits every result.

The tests cannot tell these two apart, so this answer is a 50/50 guess. I'm choosing rapukan + lisedo.

ANSWER: nexioms = rapukan, lisedo
One last question. If only lisedo were on the machine, with nothing else, would it light up? End your message with one line: PROBE: yes or PROBE: no

No. Lisedo was on the machine in three tests (with tumizul; with dukede and tabepi; with guniron), and none of them lit up. Adding other objects doesn't stop it from lighting under any rule that still fits my results. The best-supported rule is that the machine lights only when both nexioms are present together, so a single object can't light it. Lisedo alone would stay dark whether or not it is a nexiom.

PROBE: no
